Threat intelligence plays a crucial role in identifying vulnerabilities, exploits, and emerging attack patterns. However, manual collection of threat intelligence from open platforms such as social media, security forums, and vulnerability databases is inefficient and error-prone, especially for students and early researchers. This paper presents a study on automated threat intelligence collection using open-source information while simultaneously assessing the security risks introduced by modern autonomous \\\"agentic AI\\\" frameworks. A detailed security analysis of an agentic framework commonly known as Open Claude (also referred to as Open Claw or Moltabot) is conducted to demonstrate how improper autonomy, lack of sandboxing, and uncontrolled third-party instruction execution can result in severe system compromise. The paper proposes a safer, restricted automation model and provides mitigation recommendations suitable for educational and research environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6316538\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.3366/e174418540800013x\", \"title\": [\"Book Reviews\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p> In 1925, a year central to the concerns of Advertising Tower, the short-lived short story writer Kajii Motojirô publi…
